dial.summary: Risk Off emerges heading into the Sep 16 FOMC decision, with 10Y TIPS real yields confirmed at 2.55% (headwind, +16bps 4-week rise), an 85% hike probability from CME FedWatch, and BTC dominance shedding 2.7pp on Sep 13 (59.2% → 56.5%); TOTAL crypto pulled back to $2.74T and stablecoin dominance ticked up to 11.2%, signaling cautious capital rotation within crypto ahead of the synchronized global central bank decision cluster (FOMC Sep 16, BOE Sep 17, BOJ Sep 18).

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June 2026 G4 M2 at $102.66T; US M2 alone reached $23.16T in June 2026 (+5.6% YoY, 28th consecutive monthly increase, per GlobalMktObserv); 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.66T → July ~$103.4T = +$0.74T, above flat threshold); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); September monetary policy context: ECB hiked Sep 10, FOMC Sep 16 with 85% hike probability (CME FedWatch, Sep 12), BOE Sep 17, BOJ Sep 18 — synchronized tightening cycle would apply modest G4 M2 headwinds via higher reserve costs and reduced central bank asset purchases through Q4 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp (no new ISM release since Sep 1); status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY, +0.4% MoM, Sep 11) adds cost-push pressure to manufacturing sector, though Production at 58.3% indicates robust factory output; next ISM Manufacturing release October 1 (September data); S&P Global Flash PMI Sep 23 will provide the next advance manufacturing-sector read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.09 on September 11, 2026 (last trading day; Sep 12 Saturday, Sep 13 Sunday — markets closed) — muted response to hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM) and surging FOMC hike probability (85%); 4-week trend down: ~99.60 (Aug 12) → 99.09 (Sep 11) = −0.51%, marginally above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.09 within 97.5–100 neutral band); FOMC Sep 16 hike + hawkish dot plot would test the 100 headwind threshold; BOJ Sep 18 is the primary downside DXY risk via potential yen carry unwind; DXY averaging 100.12 in August 2026 (range 98.73–101.73) suggests the Sep pull-back to 99 is meaningful but not yet decisive.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 confirmed at 2.55% on September 10, 2026 (Convex Trade / H.15 release); post-CPI (Sep 11, +3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM) bond selloff likely pushed DFII10 toward 2.60%+ on Sep 11, but that daily reading is not yet confirmed in H.15; 4-week trend up: ~2.39% (Aug 11) → 2.55% (Sep 10) = +16bps over 30 days, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); 10Y nominal ~4.97% approaching psychologically significant 5% level; FOMC Sep 16 hike would extend real yield headwind as 10Y nominal is repriced higher while inflation expectations stay elevated.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 11, 2026 close: 10Y 4.97%, 2Y 4.63%, spread = +0.34% (+34bps); 2Y surged +24bps on Sep 11 following hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM) driving FOMC hike probability to 85%; 4-week trend flat: ~+35bps (Aug 12) → +34bps (Sep 11) = −1bp over 30 days, within flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread, not steepening; supportive requires positive AND steepening; shifted from marginally supportive as bear flattening offset any prior steepening); FOMC Sep 16 hike would further compress 2s10s as the 2Y prices above current levels while the 10Y is bounded by slowing growth expectations.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T (~$6,737B) for week ending September 3, 2026 (H.4.1 confirmed); H.4.1 for week ending September 10 releases September 17, 2026 — not yet available; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 6 estimate) → $6.74T (Sep 3) = +$40B, within flat threshold; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike); FOMC Sep 16 decision will inform any policy shift on balance sheet normalization pace; next confirmed WALCL update September 17.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at +0.01% per 8h (September 9, 2026; MacroMicro confirmed); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; on Sep 13 (Sunday), BTC dominance fell sharply from 59.2% to 56.49% as TOTAL crypto pulled back to $2.74T (−0.65% on day) — the dominance drop reflects altcoins outperforming BTC intraday rather than leveraged long unwinding; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action, not leveraged long crowding).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (Sep 13, 2026; CoinGecko); total crypto market cap $2.74T (−0.65% on the day); stablecoin dominance 11.2% ($307B / $2.74T); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 → 11.2% (Sep 13) = sustained ~2–3pp decline over 30 days confirming capital deployment into risk assets; 1-day uptick from 10.9% (Sep 12) to 11.2% reflects mild TOTAL contraction (not stablecoin supply expansion) and does not reverse the 30-day trend; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply: TOTAL fell on Sep 13 while dominance ticked up, opposite of headwind trigger); BTC dominance dropped sharply from 59.2% to 56.49% on Sep 13 — notable within-crypto rotation developing ahead of FOMC.

upcoming.title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Empire State Manufacturing Business Conditions Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — one of the earliest September manufacturing reads, released the day before FOMC Decision Day; August 2026 survey showed prices paid surging to 58.6 (from 52.3 in July), signaling cost-push inflation from Middle East energy spillover; a strong September reading would reinforce the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop heading into FOMC Sep 16; a sharp decline would raise questions about manufacturing sustainability; released alongside FOMC Day 1 (two-day meeting Sep 15–16).

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET (two-day meeting Sep 15–16), press conference at 2:30 PM ET; includes updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) with dot plot; current target range 3.5%–3.75%; market-implied hike probability at 85% (CME FedWatch, Sep 12) following Aug CPI +3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM (Sep 11), Aug PPI +5.4% YoY (Sep 10), and Aug NFP +162K (Sep 4); dot plot and 2027 rate path guidance are the primary DXY, real yield, and risk-asset drivers for Q4 2026; a hike + hawkish dots would push 10Y above 5% and real yields above 2.60%, extending the headwind for risk assets including crypto.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET); prior July advance retail sales were +0.1% MoM; strong Aug NFP (+162K) suggests continued consumer income growth supporting spending; a strong retail sales print (+0.3% MoM or above) confirms Q3 consumer resilience and may reinforce the Fed's inflation-fighting case; a weak print (below 0%) would suggest consumer fatigue despite labor market strength, potentially complicating the FOMC policy calculus.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization for August 2026 at 9:15 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision; measures output of manufacturing, mining, and utilities; a strong reading would reinforce ISM Manufacturing's expansion signal (54.6 in August); capacity utilization approaching 80% would add to inflationary pressures and potentially reinforce the FOMC hike case; watch energy sector output given diesel prices surging +24.1% MoM in August (Aug PPI, Sep 10).

upcoming.title: Bank of England Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee rate decision at 12:00 PM London time (7:00 AM ET) — one day after FOMC Sep 16; BOE currently holds at 3.75% (July 30 MPC vote 6-3 to hold); UK CPI elevated at 2.9% YoY in July driven by Middle East energy spillover; with ECB having hiked Sep 10 and FOMC hike probability at 85%, a BOE hold with dovish guidance would create significant monetary policy divergence driving GBP/EUR and GBP/USD volatility; a surprise BOE hike would confirm the global tightening cycle remains synchronized and extend risk-off pressure across markets.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Housing Starts and Building Permits for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for residential construction activity; released same day as BOE decision and Philadelphia Fed; higher rates (FOMC hiking Sep 16 at 85% probability) weigh on housing affordability; a decline in starts or permits would add to evidence that elevated financing costs are cooling the housing sector; 30Y fixed mortgage rates have been elevated in the 6.5–7.5% range throughout 2026.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for national ISM Manufacturing (next release Oct 1); released alongside Housing Starts and Initial Jobless Claims; a strong Philly Fed print reinforces the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop; released the day after FOMC, so September business-sentiment reaction to the Sep 16 rate decision may begin to show; Aug CPI gasoline prices drove ~1/3 of the monthly MoM increase, which may show up in manufacturing cost pressures.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 13, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 13, 2026 — first labor market read post-FOMC Sep 16; any significant spike above 220K would amplify rate-path repricing following the FOMC decision; prior week (Sep 6) approximately 206K; released alongside BOE rate decision, Housing Starts, and Philly Fed — a dense data morning one day after the FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Bank of Japan Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting September 17–18, with Statement on Monetary Policy expected September 18 — two days after FOMC Sep 16 and one day after BOE Sep 17; BOJ has been normalizing policy in 2026 (hiked June 16); any surprise hike or hawkish commentary would strengthen JPY and potentially trigger yen-carry-trade unwinds with broad impact on global risk assets including crypto; DXY at 99.09 (neutral band 97.5–100) — a hawkish BOJ would accelerate dollar weakness; the ECB (Sep 10 hike) + FOMC (Sep 16) + BOJ (Sep 18) sequence is the most synchronized global monetary policy cluster of the cycle and will set Q4 2026 macro tone.
